correctness.rationale: Normalize the six projective lines and take the branch-unit gluing sequence. The toric part takes one value per branch, modulo the line and singular-point rescalings. On characters this is the integral incidence kernel of the connected thirteen-vertex eighteen-edge graph, of rank six. Four ordinary triple points contribute one additional unipotent dimension each. Independently suppressed the three degree-two diagonal nodes and computed in the resulting Petersen graph using the reduced incidence matrix and an integral tree basis; signs on the suppressed opposite-side edges were retained. The reconstruction in /workspace/branches/reproduce_quadrangle_independent.py gives primitive rank-two Klein-four planes with combined Smith entries (1,1,2,2,2,2), and checks all five stated integral Frobenius conjugacies with basis determinants (1,-1,-1,-1,-1). Inverting the convention for Frobenius does not alter these block types. The four-cycle rotation block is the induced sign character of the order-two subgroup, hence the indicated quadratic Weil restriction of a relative norm-one torus. The fixed line, singular-point and flag triples for the five types are (6,7,18),(2,3,4),(2,3,2),(0,1,0),(0,1,0); multiplying the first entry by q+1 and adding the second minus the third checks the stated point counts. The torus rational-point groups follow from cyclic finite-field multiplicative groups and the norm kernel. The frozen Python and output were inspected, not executed.

evidence: Use the exterior basis g_ij=(e_i-e_4) wedge (e_j-e_4) for 0<=i<j<4. The earlier displayed U has determinant of absolute value 2 and mod-two kernel spanned by the all-ones vector. Thus in rational exterior coordinates the Petersen overlattice is B + Z*(sum g_ij)/2, with B the integer exterior lattice.

The three nontrivial rational Klein-four planes have respective bases (g02+g13,g03+g12), (g01+g23,g03-g12) and (g01-g23,g02-g13), from signed permutations of opposite pairs. Each plane has two of its six coordinates identically zero, so no vector in the nonintegral half-vector coset lies in it.

The three primitive plane lattices therefore have direct sum generated by the sums and differences on the three opposite pairs. It has index 2^3 in B and hence 2^4 in the Petersen lattice. Twice B and the sum of all six basis vectors already lie in that direct sum, so the quotient is elementary 2-torsion.
